non_blocking: MOST DAMAGING FAIR OBJECTION (signal detection): on UNSOLVED problems haiku has essentially no discriminability in any format, so 'criterion shift versus discrimination loss' cannot be identified there, and the ROC analysis that the abstract cites as support for a shift toward choosing (A5/H6) has no power to tell the two apart. From exps/c3/results_a5.json (prereg.UNSOLVED), I recomputed the partial areas up to fa_max=0.359: PICKC 0.086, ISOC 0.084, chance (diagonal) 0.064. The above-chance area is therefore about 0.021 (PICK) and 0.019 (ISO), while the 95% CI on the difference is [-0.030, +0.045], more than three times either procedure's entire above-chance area. The interval admits PICK being below chance, and it admits ISO having double PICK's signal. PICK's most liberal ROC point (fa 0.667, hit 0.603) lies below the diagonal. A4 says the same: J_PICK=+0.03 (diagnosticity ratio 1.04), J_ISO=+0.12 (exps/c3/results_a4.json, haiku.UNSOLVED), J difference CI [-0.26, +0.09]. With d' near 0, the confirmed C3 effect (PICK chooses more than ISO-any accepts on all-wrong pools) is a difference in response rate under near-zero signal. It is not a lineup/relative-judgment effect in the eyewitness sense, which presupposes a memory signal that fillers are matched against. The PICK-vs-EACH question-form estimate (+0.13 [+0.01,+0.25]) points instead to a demand characteristic of the 'which one is correct' wording.

Does the paper answer it? Partly. It says J is near zero for the pick and that neither procedure 'told right from wrong well there' (main.tex:87, 89), and the abstract says the pick 'carried almost no information'. But main.tex:92 ('Within these limits the two procedures trace the same curve, and pooled picking sits at a more liberal point on it') and the abstract (main.tex:19, 'This is consistent with a shift toward choosing: in a confidence-based lineup ROC the two procedures were indistinguishable') present H6 as positive support for the criterion account. In this regime both curves lie near the chance diagonal, and the test could not have distinguished a shift from a discrimination loss. Requested fix (wording, not new data): report each procedure's pAUC next to the chance pAUC, say that the H6 interval exceeds the above-chance area, and restate the reading as 'both procedures are near chance on these problems, so whether pooling shifts the criterion or lowers discrimination is not identifiable there'. Drop 'trace the same curve'.

Experiment that would test it: rerun the A4/A5 arms (PICKC, ISOC, EACH with confidence) where discriminability is intermediate rather than near 0 or near ceiling. Natural candidates are the MIXED stratum (problems solved in 1 of 2 attempts, never judged; main.tex:51) or newly sourced problems with haiku solve rate 0.3 to 0.6 from the same competitions as the other strata, which would also break the source/competence entanglement. Add a payoff manipulation (for example, a stated cost for a wrong pick versus NONE) to get several operating points per procedure, and pre-register an equivalence margin on the pAUC difference, scaled to the above-chance area, so that 'indistinguishable' becomes a testable claim. Add a wording control for PICK ('Is any of these correct? If so, which?') to separate demand from presentation.

Label-noise check, done by this reviewer: UNSOLVED ground truth is almost entirely arXiv-derived, so noise in MathArena's official grades could alone push J toward 0. 11 of 90 UNSOLVED TA pools contain parser-artifact 'wrong' answers ('<function N at 0x...>', '(inf+0j)', 'dmin'; banks/locked_c3/pools.json). I spot-read 7 of them. In every case the boxed answer really is wrong (N against gold N(N-1)/2 or 2(N-1); infinity against 29, n+5 or 30581/13860; d*min(a,1) against d*min(4a/(2+d),1); 24/pi^2 X^2 against 27/pi^2 X^2), so the labels hold up. However, arxivmath-0326_30 and arxivmath-0426_18 each have two candidates with the same answer N, because deduplication went by the parsed string (a function repr). main.tex:116 calls these 'mathematically equivalent wrong answers in different forms', but they are identical boxed answers. Worth correcting the wording.

Generality: one subject model (haiku), one vendor, math final answers only, and n=78 to 90 UNSOLVED problems. The primary pre-registered interaction (H1) is inconclusive, and the cross-model result (H3) is a non-detection. The confirmed findings (H1u, H2u) are honestly scoped, but they amount to a modest single-model result. That fits a workshop paper or a borderline main-track paper, not a flagship one.

H2u (select-then-verify) holds up better as a contribution: it is a within-model correlated-error result that does not depend on lineup framing. Reframing the paper around it plus the 'pick is uninformative beyond competence' result would be more defensible than the eyewitness analogy.
